title: Stafford's conjecture: Section 3, paper beside Lean

generator.note: v2/extract.mjs and v2/build.mjs at this commit (branch sbs-gen-sec3-20261103: side-by-side-v2 plus two fixes: the proof states of every traced declaration of a module are kept, and Lean-added steps stay in place after a prose sentence) produce sec3.extraction.json and the reader.

entries.note: Lean defines A_n(k) as the free algebra on x_i, ∂_i modulo the commutator relations given by the standard symplectic matrix; PresentedWeyl is the same algebra.

Lean writes A_n(k) as the Mathlib-only quotient Stafford38Challenge.WeylAlg k n and the moreover clause as the fixed-source statement with F = ℓ^{deg_B d} for a linear symplectic coordinate ℓ; the printed proof is Section 6, outside this slice.
Lean indexes the paper's A_n(k), n ≥ 1, as PresentedWeyl k (n + 1), and proves the stated relations and the normal form instead of citing them.
Lean indexes the filtration by ℕ with F_{-1} = 0 implicit, and defines the degree and symbol for every element, the paper only for a ≠ 0.
Lean defines both filtrations as spans of ordered PBW words of bounded weight and proves gr A_n(k) ≅ k[x, ξ] (cited by the paper).
Lean takes T*X to be Spec k[x, ξ] and states the projection and fibres on closed points K^{2n}.
Lean proves the independence of the good filtration that the paper cites from [HTT, Lemma D.3.1].
Lean states Gabber's theorem for a good order filtration of a finitely generated module and proves it; theorem_2_11_cyclic is the case A_n(K)/I used later.

lean_only.note: Iterated Ore-extension construction A_n(k) = C[p; δ], used to prove the normal form of Notation 2.2 that the paper cites from Coutinho, Prop. 1.2.1.
Isomorphism between the presented Weyl algebra and the iterated Ore construction, with its generators; the paper identifies the two without comment.

Weights of the generators and the spans of ordered monomials of bounded weight that define the Bernstein and order filtrations.
Principal component of an element, used to identify gr A_n(k) with k[x, ξ].
Strict lower pieces and principal components on a filtration piece, used to identify gr A_n(k) with k[x, ξ].
Universal property of the free-algebra presentation of A_n(k).
Weight 1 on the fibre coordinates ξ_i and 0 on x_i, which defines the order filtration.
The quotient Q = A_n(k)/I with the filtration Q_m = qF_m, its graded pieces and associated graded module.
The associated graded module of Q = A_n(k)/I for the order filtration.
The pairing Σ_i (u_{ξ_i} v_{x_i} − u_{x_i} v_{ξ_i}) on k^{2n} from which ω is built.
Right ideals of A_n(k) as submodules of the regular right module, and the quotient module A_n(k)/I.
The graded piece F_j/F_{j−1}.
Graded piece of A_n(k) identified with the homogeneous polynomials of that weight.
The map a ↦ qa from A_n(k) to a module M.
The class q of 1 in A_n(k)/I.
The filtration Q_m = qF_m of Q = A_n(k)/I.
The associated graded module as a module over k[x, ξ].
Project abbreviation for the coefficient of a monomial in a multivariate polynomial.
Generators x_i, ∂_i, their index type, the standard symplectic matrix and the relations of the Mathlib-only formulation.
Generators, ordered monomials, Bernstein pieces and linear changes of generators used to state the moreover clause in the Mathlib-only formulation.
Linear combinations of generators and the generator map of the free-algebra presentation.
The images Σ_j M_ij u_j of the generators satisfy the Weyl relations when M is symplectic.
An ω-preserving linear map of 𝕍 has a matrix in Sp(2n, k).
The matrix of the Weyl relations [∂_i, x_j] = δ_ij on generators indexed by Fin n ⊕ Fin n.
The algebra automorphism of A_n(k) given by a symplectic matrix and its inverse on generators.
The algebra endomorphism of A_n(k) that substitutes Σ_j M_ij u_j for the generator u_i.
The point of k^{2n} with coordinate 1 at one index and 0 elsewhere (e_p for the index of ∂₁).
The right ideal dA + x^N dA generated by two elements.
